sections.skill: Identify what an operating agreement should cover

questions.prompt: Which topic belongs in an operating agreement?

choices.text: What happens if an owner wants to leave
The menu for the office holiday party
The color scheme for the company website
Which social media app to post on first

questions.correct_answer: What happens if an owner wants to leave
questions.intro: An operating agreement is a written document among an LLC's owners (members) that sets the rules for running the business. It usually covers: who owns what percentage; who makes which decisions; how profits and losses are shared; what happens if an owner wants to leave, becomes unable to work, or dies; how new owners can join; and how disagreements are settled. Even a one-owner LLC can benefit from one. Some states require it. Writing it while everyone gets along prevents painful arguments later.
questions.feedback: Exit rules are a core part of an operating agreement.

questions.prompt: An operating agreement is most like what?
questions.intro: Think of roommates writing house rules: who pays which bills, who cleans, what happens if someone moves out, and how to settle arguments. Writing them on move-in day is easy; writing them during a fight is hard. An operating agreement is the house rules for the owners of an LLC: ownership, decisions, money, leaving, and disagreements.
questions.feedback: It sets rules for those who share something.
